pr.title: Switch to banker's rounding and add invoice discounts
pr.head: feature/bankers-rounding
pr.author: dana

orientation: Touches four modules. The risky one is money: roundToCents now rounds ties to the even cent (banker's rounding), a silent behaviour change in a public function that three other repos call. Invoice totals also move: VAT is rounded once per rate instead of per line, and the new discount path has no tests.

nodes.label: money

risk.why: Holds roundToCents, the riskiest change in this PR.

nodes.summary: Where fractional cents become whole ones. This PR changes the default rounding for every caller and threads a rounding mode through Money.multiply, so anything that multiplies money (VAT, discounts, three other repos) can move by a cent on a tie. Start here.

nodes.label: roundToCents()

risk.why: The default behaviour of a public function changes, and three other repos call it.

nodes.summary: Ties now round to the even cent instead of away from zero: 12.5 cents becomes 12, not 13, so VAT on a €1.50 line in Germany drops from 29 to 28 cents. A new optional mode argument ('half-up') restores the old behaviour. Three other repos call this function and will change silently when they upgrade: check whether they should pin 'half-up', and whether changing a public default needs a major version.

nodes.label: Money.multiply()

risk.why: A small pass-through diff, but checkout-web calls it and its results change on ties.

nodes.summary: Now takes an optional rounding mode and passes it on to roundToCents; when it is omitted, the new half-even default applies. The code change is mechanical, but every caller inherits the new rounding: VAT, percentage discounts and checkout-web. Check that none of them relied on ties rounding up.

nodes.label: Money.allocate()

risk.why: Unchanged, but untested code is now on the discount path.

nodes.summary: Unchanged. Splits an amount into parts proportional to a list of ratios without losing a cent, handing leftover cents to the first parts. Invoice.total now uses it to spread a discount across VAT rates, and no test covers it.

nodes.label: invoice

risk.why: Changes how totals are computed and adds new, untested money logic.

nodes.summary: Two changes: Invoice.total rounds VAT once per rate on the whole invoice instead of per line, and a new discount.ts adds promotion codes. Both change the amounts customers are charged. The existing invoice tests still pass, but none of them would catch either change.

nodes.label: Invoice.total()

risk.why: Changes the totals customers are charged, and no test covers the new rounding.

nodes.summary: VAT is now rounded once per VAT rate across the whole invoice instead of on every line, and an optional discount code is taken off before VAT. Totals can shift by a few cents on long invoices: two €1.50 lines in Germany used to carry 29 + 29 cents of VAT, now 57. invoice.test.ts was not updated and its cases give the same result under both rules, so nothing pins the new behaviour. The returned totals also gain a discount field.

nodes.label: applyDiscount()

risk.why: New money arithmetic with no tests.

nodes.summary: New: turns a discount code into an amount off the net subtotal, capped at the subtotal. Percentage codes go through Money.multiply, so half-even rounding applies (25% of €10.02 is €2.50, not €2.51). Fixed codes are a bare number of cents with no currency, so FIVEOFF takes 500 pence off a GBP invoice and 500 cents off a EUR one. No test exercises this function.

nodes.label: findDiscount()

risk.why: A simple lookup, tested for the unknown-code case.

nodes.summary: New. Looks up one of three hard-coded promotion codes, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. Because the codes live in source, changing a promotion means shipping a release. Only the unknown-code path is tested, through the handler.

nodes.label: tax

risk.why: Additive and covered by updated tests.

nodes.summary: Adds an 'ebook' VAT category with reduced rates for Germany (7%) and France (5.5%); other countries fall back to their standard rate. The change is contained and tested.

nodes.label: vatRate()

risk.why: Additive and tested: only the new 'ebook' input behaves differently.

nodes.summary: Gains an 'ebook' category: 7% in Germany and 5.5% in France via a new EBOOK_RATES table, otherwise the country's standard rate. Existing categories are unchanged, and new tests pin both the reduced rates and the fallback. Worth asking whether standard is really the right rate for e-books in GB and NL, or just a default nobody chose.

nodes.label: computeVat()

risk.why: Unchanged; it passes the rounding change through to VAT.

nodes.summary: Unchanged. Multiplies a net amount by the rate from vatRate and rounds through Money.multiply. It is the bridge from invoices to roundToCents, which is why VAT picks up half-even rounding without this file changing.

nodes.label: api

risk.why: A small additive change behind an endpoint another repo calls.

nodes.summary: POST /invoices accepts an optional discountCode and now returns a discount field with its totals. The mobile app calls this endpoint.

nodes.label: createInvoiceHandler()

risk.why: Additive and tested, but mobile-app reads its response.

nodes.summary: Accepts an optional discountCode: unknown codes get a 400, known ones are passed to Invoice.total. The JSON response now always includes a discount field (0.00 when no code is given). mobile-app calls this endpoint, so check that its response parsing tolerates the new field and that the totals it displays still match the server's after the rounding changes.

nodes.label: acme/checkout-web

risk.why: Calls two symbols whose rounding changes.

nodes.summary: Calls roundToCents and Money.multiply in src/cart/totals.ts to price the cart. After upgrading, cart totals change on half-cent ties unless it pins 'half-up', and they can disagree with invoices if the two upgrade at different times.

nodes.label: acme/payouts-service
nodes.summary: Calls roundToCents in src/payouts/fees.ts to compute fees. Fees change on ties after upgrading; check whether payouts have to match amounts already reported to partners.

nodes.label: acme/reporting
nodes.summary: Calls roundToCents in src/revenue/daily.ts to total daily revenue. The same day's figures can differ by a cent before and after the upgrade, which matters if reports are reconciled against older exports.

nodes.label: acme/mobile-app

risk.why: Calls the invoice endpoint over HTTP.

nodes.summary: Calls POST /invoices from src/api/invoices.ts. The response gains a discount field and totals can shift by a cent; it is unaffected only if its JSON decoding ignores unknown fields.
